svg.text: MOTOPROPONENT
DUOTONE ROTATIONAL LOCKUP — STUDY SHEET
the word, plus the same word rotated 180° in a second colour · read one hue or the other
ONE READING ALONE
layer A by itself — proper letterforms, nothing compromised, nothing carried by context
BOTH READINGS
red reads upright · teal reads upside-down · the pivot O sits on the axis so both layers draw it in the same place
THE SAME ARTWORK, ROTATED 180°
identical geometry with the hues swapped — now teal reads upright
TREATMENTS
how hard the second reading pushes is a dial, not a given
equal value — neither reading wins
ink primary, accent secondary — upright dominates
ink primary, hairline secondary — the second reading is a watermark
SIZE TEST
two overlaid words is twice the ink — this is where it gives out
900px wide
520px wide
300px wide
NOTES
• Colour is load-bearing. Flattened to one ink the two layers tangle, so this needs a monochrome fallback — the flat ambigram, or the word set in type.
• Layout is unconstrained: the composite is symmetric for ANY layout, because rotating it just swaps the two layers. Widths and tracking are purely optical here.
• Tracking is looser across N-E-N-T than across the round-heavy first half. That is optically correct anyway, and it is what puts the pivot O on the rotation axis.
• mix-blend-mode may not survive an Illustrator round-trip; reapply Multiply to the second layer there, or set it as a transparency-group blend on export.
